about.title: Escondido Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: In 2025, Escondido recorded 10 traffic deaths on its streets and freeways, according to public collision records. Ten is a small number on a spreadsheet. For the families behind it, each one reshaped a household on a single day. Some of those crashes happened along Valley Parkway, on I-15, or near Washington and Mission Avenues, the corridors where the city's collision reports cluster most often, frequently on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Not every wrongful death in Escondido involves a vehicle. A fall at a job site, a defective product, or a fatal medical error can also give rise to a claim under California law. What ties these cases together is that a family is left to cover funeral costs and carry on without the income, care, and guidance the person provided. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects San Diego County families with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death claims on a contingency basis, so you can ask questions without adding a bill to an already hard season.

whyChoose.title: What Escondido Families Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Only certain family members can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim. A spouse or domestic partner and children come first; if none survive, certain dependents and heirs may have standing, and an attorney can confirm where your family fits.

items.title: The clock is two years, sometimes less
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death. If a city, county, or state agency may share responsibility, a much shorter government claim deadline applies, so early contact matters.

items.title: Losses go beyond the funeral bill
items.desc: Recoverable damages can include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. This civil claim is separate from any criminal case.

items.question: The crash that killed my family member was on I-15 near Escondido. Does that change who I file against?
items.answer: It can. A freeway crash may involve the other driver, an employer if a work vehicle was involved, or in some cases a public agency responsible for the roadway. Claims against a government entity carry a much shorter filing window than the standard two years, so it is worth having an attorney review the facts soon.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves separately from any criminal prosecution. The criminal case can affect the evidence available, but your family does not have to wait for a verdict to begin protecting your rights, and the two-year deadline continues to run regardless.

items.question: What does it cost to speak with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and the independent attorneys in our network handle wrongful death claims on contingency. That means no fee unless there is a recovery, and the first conversation is simply a chance to ask questions.
